title: Weighted-lane policy for pricing exceptions and invoice fulfillment
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a prescriptive weighted-lane decision policy to intake, prioritize, and fulfill non-bug pricing and billing requests (commitments, invoicing exceptions, cost allocation questions, and marketplace offsets). The goal is a repeatable operational play that reduces time-to-response for enterprise requests, clarifies negotiation ownership, and ensures consistent accounting treatment for marketplace credits and commitment discounts.
context_and_problem_statement: We currently get ad hoc emails and Zendesk tickets for pricing concessions, invoice corrections, and marketplace offset asks. These requests bounce between GTM, Finance, Legal, and Product and often lack consistent metadata (customer tier, ARR impact, contract terms). That causes long SLAs, duplicated work, and inconsistent cost accounting. We need a weighted-lane policy that forces consistent intake fields, assigns preliminary ownership, and prescribes SLA & escalation behavior based on objective signals.
acceptance_criteria: A structured intake form (Zendesk + internal intake) capturing required metadata: customer tier, contract ref, requested adjustment type, financial impact estimate, legal dependencies, desired timeline.
A weighted-lane decision matrix mapping requests to response SLA (e.g., 48h triage, 7-day proposal, 30-day negotiation) and primary owner (GTM/Finance/Product) based on signals.
Clear delegation rules for low-dollar requests to CS with guardrails; medium/high-dollar requests routed to PM + Finance review.
A sample handoff checklist and templated email/PRD to be used when escalating to sales/legal/finance.
Operational dashboard widget in Redwood Console for tracking open pricing requests by lane and SLA status (mockup and API spec linked).
high_level_solution_outline: 1) Intake: enforce a 12-field intake form surfaced in Zendesk + internal catalog; 2) Scoring: compute a weighted score from signals (ARR impact, churn risk, strategic customer, compliance/regulatory requirement, contract complexity); 3) Lanes: map score ranges to lanes (Self-serve CS, Standard GTM, Escalation Board); 4) SLA & playbooks: define triage/response timelines and templates per lane; 5) Telemetry: track SLA compliance and downstream accounting tags for marketplace offsets.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: How do we reliably estimate ARR impact at intake without Finance involvement? (proposal: provide conservative bands and require Finance sign-off above threshold)
Should marketplace offsets follow same lanes as invoice corrections or be treated as their own flow? (proposal: separate lane if involvement requires 3rd-party marketplace accounting)
Does enabling delegation to CS increase risk of incorrect discounts being applied? Need guardrail checks and post-hoc audits.
Timeline alignment with Finance close cycles: some invoice fixes must adhere to monthly close deadlines which constrain SLA feasibility.
implementation_tasks: Draft intake form fields + validation rules (Priya)
Define weighted scoring algorithm and default weights (Product + Finance)
Create lane definitions and SLA table (Ops)
Build Zendesk intake workflow + zap to internal ticketing (Eng/Revenue Ops)
Design dashboard mock and metrics (Design + Data)
Author templated responses and escalation checklist (Legal + Sales)
Pilot the flow with 10 live requests for 30 days and collect metrics (CS + PM)
Rollout training and runbook to GTM and CS teams (PM)
